newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya capital calm after student unrest.
newsitem.headline: Kenya capital calm after student unrest.

text.p: The Kenyan capital of Nairobi was calm early on Tuesday after five people were injured in clashes between riot police and students angry over university conditions and demanding constitutional reform.

In Mombasa Moslem preacher Sheikh Balala, a fierce critic of President Daniel arap Moi, said he would tour the city and visit schools on Tuesday, after returning from two years in exile, witnesses said.
Kenya Polytechnic students seized control of Haile Selassie Avenue, a major highway through Nairobi city centre, for hours on Monday, stoning cars and police and burning tyres.
Two students, two passers-by and a journalist were injured as police wielding batons and firing live ammunition and teargas moved onto the campus.
The clashes were confined to Haile Selassie Avenue and did not halt business in central Nairobi, unlike disturbances last Monday in the capital and other towns and cities.
Nine people were killed last Monday in the most serious civil disturbances since a 1990 campaign to press for constitutional reforms.
The students were protesting against a new bill that provided for expulsion for non-payment of fees and revised charges for exams. They also demanded constitutional reform.
Fourteen people were arrested during the disturbances and would be charged on Tuesday, police said. There were no police casualties.
Opposition-backed groups have campaigned since April for constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections this year. No date is set for the polls.
The reforms would reduce the power of Moi, 73 and in power since 1978, who is widely expected to win elections against an opposition that has found a fragile cohesion in reform demands.

Moi said last Friday he would take action against any attempt to bring chaos to the country and challenged the opposition to take the debate on reforms to parliament, where his ruling party has a majority.
Balala returned to Kenya on Saturday from exile in Germany vowing to spearhead a reform campaign.
"I don't recognise the forthcoming elections and I would rather voters burned their registration cards," Balala told a crowd of around 1,000 at the Sakina Mosque in the Indian Ocean port.
His aides said a planned "illegal" rally in Mombasa on Tuesday had been called off.
Authorities ordered Nairobi University and Jomo Kenyatta University closed indefinitely last week and students were sent home following days of clashes with riot police in the capital.
